 Turn an old Android phone into a desk panel for your computer. 
PC stats, AI coding sessions, music and touch controls over USB or Wi-Fi. 
Windows, Linux and macOS. No root, PhoneBox account or cloud service required. 

 
 Try the live demo ·
 Download ·
 Quick start 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 Example layouts with demo data. 

PhoneBox pairs a full-screen Android app with a small desktop agent . Build your panel in a browser-based
visual editor: 132 widgets , 30 templates , multiple pages and a live preview. Connect several phones with
their own layouts, or switch one phone between paired computers.

 What you can do

 Use it for What appears on the phone 
 --- --- 
 PC monitoring CPU, GPU, RAM, disks, network and ping; charts, GPU details and process controls 
 AI coding Claude, Codex and Antigravity quotas, reset times and burn-rate forecasts; local Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode sessions (native and inside WSL); GitHub reviews and CI status 
 Touch controls App and URL shortcuts, key combinations and macros; application audio, microphone, media, OBS and system controls through Control Deck 
 Everyday use Now Playing, internet radio, clocks, weather, calendars, notes, checklists, pomodoro and timers 
 Automation Webhook values and notifications, Home Assistant controls and rules that react to activity on the computer 

Tap an AI session for its model, timing and token details. Opt in to Codex, Claude Code or OpenCode permission prompts
to answer Allow , Deny (and Always allow for OpenCode) from the phone. Optional
CodexBar integration adds quota providers and a cost overview.

 
 A tour with demo data: notifications, permission prompts and automatic page switching. Watch the MP4 

 Quick start

You need an Android 5+ phone (Android 6 or later recommended) and a supported computer. USB uses a data cable and USB debugging; Wi-Fi pairing
works without either. Release agents include .NET, so you do not need to install the runtime.

 1. Install the desktop agent

 Windows 10/11 x64 — paste into a normal PowerShell window:

 

 Linux or macOS — run as your own user:

 

Setup downloads the latest release, checks its SHA-256 checksum, offers missing dependencies and start-at-login,
and opens the settings at . It can also install the Android app over USB.
Run setup again to update or repair the installation while keeping settings and pairings.

 Windows signing: release agents are still unsigned: SignPath Foundation accepted PhoneBox and test signing works, and releases are signed once its release certificate is issued.
 SmartScreen or antivirus software may warn or block them. See the code signing policy
 and installation warnings. USB debugging should be authorized only on computers you trust.

Read the scripts before running them: Windows · Linux/macOS.
The installation guide covers options, dependencies, install paths, troubleshooting and uninstalling.

 2. Connect the phone

 USB Wi-Fi only 
 --- --- 
 Enable Developer options → USB debugging , connect a data cable and accept the phone's authorization prompt. Let setup install the app, or use Settings → General → Install the phone app . Install the APK from the latest release. Wi-Fi is off by default: open the settings page (tray icon, or turn on General → Wi-Fi & Tailscale → Let the phone connect without the USB cable , click Save , then Restart to apply at the top. Choose Pair a phone over Wi-Fi , scan the pairing QR code and confirm the matching check code. 
 Wakes and opens the panel on connection; supports app updates over adb. No adb or developer options needed; install app updates manually unless you later configure USB. 

The phone app is not in any app store; it comes only from this repository's releases. It runs on Android 5.0 and
newer; there is no iOS version.

For automatic USB/Wi-Fi fallback, enable Wi-Fi and connect the phone over USB once.
Connection details and Tailscale setup →

 3. Make it yours

Open (or double-click the Windows tray icon). Under Pages , choose a template, drag and
resize widgets, then Save . Use Live preview to see unsaved edits with live data.
Swipe, tap the page dots or use the phone's volume keys to move between pages.

 
 Other installation methods 

- Manual download: unzip the agent for your system from the release page
 and run it. Install the APK on the phone. Checksums and build provenance accompany the release assets.
- Scoop (Windows): 

 

- From source: see the installation guide and development guide.
- winget: manifests are prepared in packaging/winget; see the installation guide for details.

 

 Pages & templates

Start with Home, System, AI quotas, Sessions, Music, Planner, Automation or a Control Deck template, then adapt the
12 × 6 grid to your phone. Portrait and landscape layouts are supported. Smart Stack puts up to 12 widgets in one slot.

 Home AI sessions 
 --- --- 
 
 System Layout editor 
 

Screenshots use demo data. Browse the template gallery and widgets.
Change fonts, size, spacing, corners and surfaces globally or for one page or widget with the appearance guide.

 Platform support

 Windows Linux macOS 
 --- --- --- --- 
 Release builds x64 x64 / ARM64, glibc Apple silicon / Intel 
 CPU, RAM, disks, network, processes ✓ ✓ ✓ 
 GPU data Windows counters; NVIDIA via nvidia-smi ; extra sensors via LibreHardwareMonitor NVIDIA / AMD; Intel clock Apple silicon, when exposed by macOS 
 Media System media sessions playerctl nowplaying-cli ; Spotify / Music fallback 
 Volume Native wpctl / pactl System output; availability varies by device 
 Agent interface Tray icon + browser settings Browser settings Browser settings 

Widgets depend on the host's hardware, installed tools and permissions. Advanced

install.title: Quick start
install.html:
You need an Android 5+ phone (Android 6 or later recommended) and a supported computer. USB uses a data cable and USB debugging; Wi-Fi pairing works without either. Release agents include .NET, so you do not need to install the runtime.

1. Install the desktop agent

Windows 10/11 x64 — paste into a normal PowerShell window:

irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ersinkoc/phonebox/main/setup.ps1 | iex

Linux or macOS — run as your own user:

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ersinkoc/phonebox/main/setup.sh | bash

Setup downloads the latest release, checks its SHA-256 checksum, offers missing dependencies and start-at-login, and opens the settings at http://127.0.0.1:8765. It can also install the Android app over USB. Run setup again to update or repair the installation while keeping settings and pairings.

Windows signing: release agents are still unsigned: SignPath Foundation accepted PhoneBox and test signing works, and releases are signed once its release certificate is issued. SmartScreen or antivirus software may warn or block them. See the code signing policy and installation warnings. USB debugging should be authorized only on computers you trust.

Read the scripts before running them: Windows · Linux/macOS. The installation guide covers options, dependencies, install paths, troubleshooting and uninstalling.

2. Connect the phone
USB Wi-Fi only
Enable Developer options → USB debugging, connect a data cable and accept the phone's authorization prompt. Let setup install the app, or use Settings → General → Install the phone app. Install the APK from the latest release. Wi-Fi is off by default: open the settings page (tray icon, or http://127.0.0.1:8765), turn on General → Wi-Fi & Tailscale → Let the phone connect without the USB cable, click Save, then Restart to apply at the top. Choose Pair a phone over Wi-Fi, scan the pairing QR code and confirm the matching check code.
Wakes and opens the panel on connection; supports app updates over adb. No adb or developer options needed; install app updates manually unless you later configure USB.

The phone app is not in any app store; it comes only from this repository's releases. It runs on Android 5.0 and newer; there is no iOS version.

For automatic USB/Wi-Fi fallback, enable Wi-Fi and connect the phone over USB once. Connection details and Tailscale setup →

3. Make it yours

Open http://127.0.0.1:8765 (or double-click the Windows tray icon). Under Pages, choose a template, drag and resize widgets, then Save. Use Live preview to see unsaved edits with live data. Swipe, tap the page dots or use the phone's volume keys to move between pages.

Other installation methods

  • Manual download: unzip the agent for your system from the release page and run it. Install the APK on the phone. Checksums and build provenance accompany the release assets.

  • Scoop (Windows):

    scoop bucket add phonebox https://github.com/ersinkoc/phonebox
scoop install main/adb phonebox/phonebox

  • From source: see the installation guide and development guide.

  • winget: manifests are prepared in packaging/winget; see the installation guide for details.
